original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-inverse-limit-complexes}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let
$(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet)$ be an inverse system of complexes of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules. Let $m \in \mathbf{Z}$. Suppose given
$\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and an integer
$n_0$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering whose members are
elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item for every $U \in \mathcal{B}$
\begin{enumerate}
\item the systems of abelian groups
$\mathcal{F}_n^{m - 2}(U)$ and $\mathcal{F}_n^{m - 1}(U)$
have vanishing $R^1\lim$ (for example these have the Mittag-Leffler property),
\item the system of abelian groups $H^{m - 1}(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet(U))$
has vanishing $R^1\lim$ (for example it has the Mittag-Leffler property), and
\item we have
$H^m(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet(U)) = H^m(\mathcal{F}_{n_0}^\bullet(U))$
for all $n \geq n_0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then the maps $H^m(\mathcal{F}^\bullet) \to \lim H^m(\mathcal{F}_n^\bullet)
\to H^m(\mathcal{F}_{n_0}^\bullet)$ are isomorphisms of sheaves where
$\mathcal{F}^\bullet = \lim \mathcal{F}_n^\bullet$ is the termwise
inverse limit.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
Let $(\mathcal F_n^\bullet)$ be an inverse system of complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules on a ringed site, and let $\mathcal F^\bullet=\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n^\bullet$ be their **termwise** inverse limit. For a site object $U$, $H^m(\mathcal F_n^\bullet(U))$ is cohomology of the complex of **sections** over $U$, while $H^m(\mathcal F_n^\bullet)$ is the **cohomology sheaf**. The $R^1\varprojlim$ conditions below concern inverse systems of groups of sections; the final map is an isomorphism of sheaves. This is a technical lemma about an ordinary limit, not an assumption that ordinary and derived limits coincide automatically.

hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site and $(\mathcal F_n^\bullet)$ an inverse system of complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules.
$m\in\mathbf Z$, $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathrm{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ covers all site objects, and $n_0$ is an index.
For every $U\in\mathcal B$ and every $n\ge n_0$, the transition comparison $H^m(\mathcal F_n^\bullet(U))\to H^m(\mathcal F_{n_0}^\bullet(U))$ is an isomorphism.
conclusions: For $\mathcal F^\bullet=\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n^\bullet$ (termwise limit), both canonical maps of cohomology sheaves $H^m(\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\varprojlim_nH^m(\mathcal F_n^\bullet)\to H^m(\mathcal F_{n_0}^\bullet)$ are isomorphisms.
